solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: the servant cuts through the middle of BE, so sits inside it

blocks.note: to be = to live, to exist
a lackey is a servant or footman

annotation.surface: A laboratory servant cutting open a living mouse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mouse' looks like the rodent under the knife; it is slang for a bruise round the eye. LACKEY goes inside B...E.
annotation.definitionFit: A mouse is informal slang for a black eye, the swelling looking like a small dark lump.

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up or include, so BUD holds STAR

blocks.note: a bud is a young shoot on a plant
star as an adjective: a star player is a celebrated one

annotation.surface: A photo shoot featuring a famous bird.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' suggests firing a gun or a photo session; here it is the plant's shoot. 'Celebrated' must be read as an adjective, STAR.
annotation.definitionFit: The bustard is a large ground-dwelling game bird of open plains.

entries.clue: Port, rum, beer and last of wine (8)

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the letters go strange
takes the final letter of the word that follows

annotation.surface: A drinks order: port, rum, beer and a final glass of wine.
annotation.walkthrough: The opening list reads as a row of drinks, but port is the definition and rum is an adjective meaning odd, not a spirit.
annotation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is a major North Sea port in north-east Scotland.

entries.clue: People in hamlet prepared Swiss cheese (9)

indicators.note: MEN goes in the rearranged HAMLET
prepared means made ready, worked into a new form

annotation.surface: Villagers in a small hamlet making Swiss cheese.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' tempts a Shakespeare reading, but it is just six letters to rearrange around MEN.
annotation.definitionFit: Emmenthal is the hard Swiss cheese with large holes.

indicators.note: only part of the next word is used

blocks.note: the three letters after FI in fiendish

annotation.surface: A plan with a slightly evil aim.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Somewhat' reads as a softener for 'fiendish'; it marks that only part of that word is wanted.
annotation.definitionFit: An end is an aim or purpose, as in 'to that end'.

indicators.note: H runs away, leaving the word

blocks.note: h = husband, the abbreviation in family trees
a shack is a rough cabin; its H is the one that flees

annotation.surface: A husband runs from a burning cabin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cabin fire' reads as a blaze; fire is the verb, to dismiss from a job.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the employment sense: both mean dismissing a worker, 'sack' from the bag of tools once handed back.

blocks.note: man = husband, as in 'man and wife'

annotation.surface: A general's son and his wife's husband listed as family.
annotation.walkthrough: William Tecumseh Sherman was a Union general in the American Civil War.
annotation.definitionFit: Sherman was a famous American Civil War general, whose name was later given to a tank.

entries.clue: Part of church with luck found on left (7)

indicators.note: L is placed next, on the end of CHANCE

annotation.surface: Someone finds a lucky spot on the left side of a church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Found on' only places L after CHANCE; with it, 'with' is just a joining word.
annotation.definitionFit: The chancel is the part of a church near the altar, where the clergy and choir sit.

indicators.note: a covering lies over and around what it hides, so SET goes round U

blocks.note: U is Uniform in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Solidified fat forming a coat over a uniform.
annotation.walkthrough: S(U)ET. 'Solidified' seems to describe the fat, but it is its own piece of wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Suet is the hard fat from around an animal's kidneys, used in British puddings and pastry.

indicators.note: the letters are made to suffer, knocked out of shape

annotation.surface: An old-fashioned man called Levi is made to suffer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Made' reads as part of 'made to suffer'; it is really fodder, with 'to suffer' alone as the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Medieval is used loosely to mean hopelessly old-fashioned or obsolete.

blocks.note: a formal meeting granted by someone important, like the Pope or a monarch

annotation.surface: A press interview in front of onlookers.
annotation.walkthrough: Both words define the answer: one is granted an audience with a monarch, and an audience fills a theatre.
annotation.definitionFit: An audience is both a formal meeting with someone important and a body of spectators.

blocks.note: Ena is a woman's name, a crossword stock female

annotation.surface: Our editor has fallen for a woman and married her.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Female' has to be a specific name here, not F or HER: ENA is a favourite of setters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone struck by love, 'smitten' literally hit, 'enamoured' from the French for love.

entries.clue: Repartee, not bad in advancing years (3)

indicators.note: remove BAD IN from the word

blocks.note: badinage is witty banter; drop BAD IN

annotation.surface: Witty back-and-forth that has not faded with the years.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not bad' reads as a compliment; 'in' belongs with it, both words leaving BADINAGE to give AGE.
annotation.definitionFit: Age is the state of advancing years, as in 'the wisdom of age'.

indicators.note: MAN splits GOURD, sitting in its middle

blocks.note: a gourd is a hard-skinned fruit
to man is to staff, as in manning a desk

annotation.surface: Kitchen staff cutting fruit for a fussy diner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as a stick or as employees; here it is the verb MAN.
annotation.definitionFit: A gourmand is a lover of good food, close in sense to an epicure.

indicators.note: NERD is turned back to front
'companion after' means the companion follows, so CH is written behind the turned anorak

blocks.note: an anorak is British slang for a geek or nerd
CH = Companion of Honour, a British order

annotation.surface: Getting a friend wet after bringing back a raincoat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Anorak' looks like the waterproof jacket; in Britain it is also slang for an obsessive nerd, named after the coats trainspotters wear.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean making something wet through, drench perhaps a shade heavier.

entries.clue: Bishop in gown has line in crime (7)

indicators.note: 'Bishop in gown' puts the bishop inside the robe, as a man is in his clothes
the gown has RY added to it

annotation.surface: A bishop in his gown is caught up in a crime.
annotation.walkthrough: ROB(B)E + RY. The second 'in' is only the link to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: robbery is one particular crime among many.

entries.clue: Just arrived from north-east, Brown taken out (7)

indicators.note: BROWN is taken out and knocked about, like a boxer

annotation.surface: A new arrival from the north-east, with someone called Brown removed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taken out' sounds like a deletion or a date; here it means knocked about, so the letters of BROWN are rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective used in its literal sense: a newborn baby is one that has just arrived.

entries.clue: Right to stop an ancient poet (6)

indicators.note: R stops a gap, plugging it inside AN OLD

blocks.note: used as printed; R goes after the A

annotation.surface: Someone has the right to silence an old poet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'An ancient poet' looks like the whole definition, Homer perhaps; only 'poet' is. A(R)N OLD gives Matthew Arnold, the Victorian poet.
annotation.definitionFit: Matthew Arnold was a Victorian English poet, author of 'Dover Beach'.

indicators.note: the letters lose their bearings

annotation.surface: An actor in a strange part has lost their way while writing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Odd' reads as a description of the role; it is fodder, and 'disorientated' alone gives the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A doodler scribbles idly, making aimless drawings.

annotation.surface: The Old Norse and English languages joined together.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old Norse' is a real language, but here each word is its own abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: To be one is to be united, as in 'they spoke as one'.

indicators.note: E is fed into the rearranged letters
the letters of ORLANDO go wild

blocks.note: E = energy, as in E = mc²

annotation.surface: Energy drives a crazed Orlando who paints.
annotation.walkthrough: Orlando the name, or the Florida city, is only seven letters to rearrange, with E slipped in after the L.
annotation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci is the Renaissance artist of the Mona Lisa.

blocks.note: porter is a dark sweetish beer

annotation.surface: Someone takes a whack at a dark sweet beer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hack' reads as a verb, to chop; it is the noun, a journalist.
annotation.definitionFit: A hack is a journalist, especially a jobbing one: a reporter.

indicators.note: to pinch is to steal, so something is taken
what is taken is the last letter, the bottom in a down entry

blocks.note: tart is slang for a prostitute; lose the last T

annotation.surface: A sailor pinches a prostitute's bottom.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a crude picture; 'pinching' means stealing, so TART loses its bottom letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Tar, short for tarpaulin, is an old slang word for a sailor.

entries.clue: With everything needed to create barrier (4)

annotation.surface: A list of all the materials needed to build a barrier.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With everything' is W + ALL; 'needed to create' merely ties the wordplay to the barrier.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a wall is the commonest kind of barrier, built to keep people or things out.

indicators.note: travelling around means roaming from place to place, so the letters wander out of their order

annotation.surface: A traveller whose only tour is around a French city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Only' reads as a limiting word in the surface; it is the four letters to move around.
annotation.definitionFit: Lyon is France's third-largest city.

indicators.note: the letters are shaped into something new

annotation.surface: A CD player carved out of timber.
annotation.walkthrough: 'CD reader' looks like a piece of kit; it is just eight letters to reshape.
annotation.definitionFit: Red cedar is a reddish timber from North American and Asian trees, prized for fencing and cladding.
